# `css/no-undeclared-custom-properties`

**A custom property a stylesheet reads is declared by one that loads with it**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-css` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-css` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | CSS, SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:css/project` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `warn` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the value of the property, or a fallback, is the author's to write) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `biome/nursery/noUndeclaredCustomProperties` |

## What it checks

A `var(--name)` without a fallback names a custom property that a stylesheet loading with this one declares (`--name: …`) or registers (`@property --name`), or that a script or page of the same scope writes (`setProperty('--name', …)`, `style="--name: …"`). Loading with a stylesheet means what its entries reach, as for `js/no-undeclared-classes`. Behaviour of Biome's `noUndeclaredCustomProperties`, read from its documentation and rewritten.

**Why:** an undeclared custom property makes the declaration invalid at computed-value time, so the property falls back to its inherited or initial value and the page loses its style without an error.

`var(--name, fallback)` is not reported. A stylesheet nothing loads is left alone (whoever loads it may declare the property), and so is one with anything that cannot be read whole in its scope: a stylesheet of a package or another host, a missing Sass partial, Tailwind's directives, a property named by interpolation (`--#{$n}`). `css/no-unknown-custom-properties` reads one stylesheet; this rule reads the project.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-css
pip install codelaw-rules-css
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:css/project` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:css/project"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"css/no-undeclared-custom-properties" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css/no-undeclared-custom-properties" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"css/no-undeclared-custom-properties" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"css/no-undeclared-custom-properties" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"css/no-undeclared-custom-properties" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "css/no-undeclared-custom-properties": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-undeclared-custom-properties: <reason> */`
- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore css/no-undeclared-custom-properties: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-undeclared-custom-properties expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> */`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule css/no-undeclared-custom-properties --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain css/no-undeclared-custom-properties       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule css/no-undeclared-custom-properties  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                       # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Declare the property, in `:root` or in the rule that needs it, or give `var()` a fallback.
2. If a script sets it at run time, write its name in that script (`style.setProperty('--name', …)`): any `--name` the scope's scripts and pages write counts as declared.

## Examples

### CSS

#### Don't

```css files
/* src/a.css */
.a { color: var(--brand); }
// src/main.js
import "./a.css";
```

#### Do

```css files
/* src/a.css */
.a { color: var(--brand); }
/* src/theme.css */
:root { --brand: red; }
// src/main.js
import "./a.css";
import "./theme.css";
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss files
/* src/a.scss */
.a { color: var(--brand); }
// src/main.js
import "./a.scss";
```

#### Do

```scss files
/* src/a.scss */
.a { color: var(--brand); }
/* src/theme.scss */
:root { --brand: red; }
// src/main.js
import "./a.scss";
import "./theme.scss";
```

## Differences from the source

Biome's `noUndeclaredCustomProperties` reads the stylesheets one file imports. This rule reads what loads with the stylesheet through the project graph, counts what scripts and pages write, and stays silent when part of the scope cannot be read. Properties named in JSX `style` strings are not read.
